content.text:
Confirmed. This commit `0caa272cd1` introduced the `removeCinderDisks()` method where `failedRemoveCinderDisks` is declared `null` and, in the catch block, `.addAll()` is called on it — a NullPointerException waiting to happen. The bug-fixing commit `58902b70` simply replaces `failedRemoveCinderDisks.addAll(cinderDisks)` with `failedRemoveCinderDisks = cinderDisks`, exactly undoing this introduction.

## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: 0caa272cd1226a96acb1f6fdc0da52f6759f86ef

## Reasoning
(1) I traced the history of `RemoveVmCommand.java`, specifically the line changed by the fix (`failedRemoveCinderDisks.addAll(cinderDisks)` in a catch block). Using `git log -S` to find when `failedRemoveCinderDisks = null` was introduced located a single commit.

(2) Commit `0caa272cd1` added the new `removeCinderDisks()` method, declaring `Collection<CinderDisk> failedRemoveCinderDisks = null;`. In the `catch (InterruptedException | ExecutionException e)` block — which executes precisely when `future.get()` throws, meaning `failedRemoveCinderDisks` was never assigned and remains `null` — the code calls `failedRemoveCinderDisks.addAll(cinderDisks)`, causing a guaranteed `NullPointerException` on the exception path.

(3) This is the only commit in the file's history that introduces this variable and this exact buggy pattern (confirmed via `git log -p --follow` and `git log -S`). The fix commit `58902b70` directly reverses this specific line, changing it to a safe assignment (`failedRemoveCinderDisks = cinderDisks`), which is the standard way to fix this kind of NPE-on-null-collection bug. No other commits touch this logic in between, so I'm confident this is the sole bug-introducing commit.
